verses.text: Now e happen for di thirtieth year, for di fourth month, for di fifth day of di month, as I dey among di captives by di river Chebar, say di heavens open, and I see visions of God.
For di fifth day of di month (e na di fifth year of King Jehoiachin captivity),
di word of di Lord come expressly to Ezekiel di priest, Buzi pikin, for di land of di Chaldeans by di river Chebar. Di hand of di Lord dey dere on am.

I look, and see, whirlwind come out of di north, great cloud, with fire flashing up continually, and brightness round about am, and out of di middle of am something like glowing metal, out of di middle of di fire.
Out of di middle of am come di likeness of four living creatures. Dis na dem appearance: dem get di likeness of man.
Everyone get four faces, and everyone of dem get four wings.
Dem legs na straight legs, and di soles of dem feet like di sole of calf foot. Dem sparkle like burnished bronze.
Dem get human hands under dem wings on dem four sides. Dem four get dem faces and dem wings thus:
dem wings dey joined one to another. Dem no turn when dem go. Everyone go straight forward.
As for di likeness of dem faces, dem four get face of man, and face of lion on di right side. Dem four get face of ox on di left side. Dem four also get face of eagle.
Dem faces and dem wings dey separated above. Two wings of every one dey joined one to another, and two cover dem bodies.
Everyone go straight forward. Wherever di spirit go, dem go. Dem no turn when dem go.

As for di likeness of di living creatures, dem appearance be like burning coals of fire, like di appearance of torches. E dey go up and down among di living creatures. Di fire dey bright, and out of di fire lightning dey go out.
Di living creatures run and return like di appearance of flash of lightning.
Now as I behold di living creatures, see, one wheel dey on di earth beside di living creatures, for each of di four faces.
Di appearance of di wheels and dem work dey like beryl. Di four of dem get one likeness. Dem appearance and dem work dey as if one wheel dey inside another wheel.
When dem go, dem go on dem four sides. Dem no turn when dem go.
As for dem rims, dem dey high and dreadful. Dem four rims dey full of eyes round about.
When di living creatures go, di wheels go beside dem. When di living creatures dey lifted up from di earth, di wheels dey lifted up.
Wherever di spirit go, dem go. Dere di spirit go, and di wheels dey lifted up beside dem, because di spirit of di living creature dey for di wheels.
When dem go, di others go. When dem stand, di others stand. When dem dey lifted up from di earth, di wheels dey lifted up beside dem, because di spirit of di living creature dey for di wheels.
Over di heads of di living creatures dey likeness of firmament, like di awesome crystal, stretched out over dem heads above.
Under di firmament dem wings dey straight, one toward another. Everyone get two wings covering dis side, and everyone get two wings covering dat side, on dem bodies.
When dem go, I hear di noise of dem wings like di noise of great waters, like di voice of di Almighty, di sound of tumult like di noise of army. When dem stand, dem lower dem wings.
Voice dey above di firmament wey dey over dem heads. When dem stand, dem lower dem wings.
Above di firmament wey dey over dem heads na di likeness of throne, as di appearance of sapphire stone. On di likeness of di throne dey likeness as di appearance of man on am above.

I see as glowing metal, as di appearance of fire round about inside am, from di appearance of im waist and upward. From di appearance of im waist and downward, I see as di appearance of fire, and e get brightness round about am.

As di appearance of di rainbow wey dey for di cloud for di day of rain, so be di appearance of di brightness round about. Dis na di appearance of di likeness of di glory of di Lord. When I see am, I fall on my face, and I hear voice of one wey dey speak.
E talk to me, “Son of man, stand on your feet, and I go speak to you.”
Spirit enter me when e speak to me, and set me on my feet. I hear am wey speak to me.
E talk to me, “Son of man, I dey send you to di children of Israel, to nation of rebels wey don rebel against me. Dem and dem fathers don transgress against me, even to dis very day.
Di children dey impudent and stubborn of heart. I dey send you to dem, and you go talk to dem, ‘Di Lord God talk like dis.’
Dem, whether dem go hear, or whether dem go refuse (because dem na rebellious house), yet dem go know say prophet don dey among dem.

You, son of man, no fear dem, neither dey afraid of dem words, though briers and thorns dey with you, and you dey dwell among scorpions. No dey afraid of dem words, nor dey dismayed at dem looks, though dem na rebellious house.
You go speak my words to dem, whether dem hear or whether dem refuse, because dem na most rebellious.
But you, son of man, hear wetin I talk to you. No be rebellious like dat rebellious house. Open your mouth, and eat wetin I give you.”
When I look, see, hand dey stretched out to me, and see, scroll of book dey inside am.
E spread am before me. E dey written on di front and on di back. Lamentations, mourning and woe dey written inside am.
E talk to me, “Son of man, eat wetin you find. Eat dis scroll, and go speak to di house of Israel.”
So I open my mouth, and e cause me to eat di scroll.
E talk to me, “Son of man, cause your belly to eat, and fill your bowels with dis scroll wey I give you.” Den I eat am, and e dey as sweet as honey for my mouth.
E talk to me, “Son of man, go, get yourself to di house of Israel, and speak my words to dem.
Because you no dey sent to people of strange speech and of hard language, but to di house of Israel,
no to many peoples of strange speech and of hard language, whose words you no fit understand. Surely if I send you to dem, dem for listen to you.
But di house of Israel no go listen to you, because dem no go listen to me, because all di house of Israel dey hard of forehead and hardened of heart.
See, I don make your face hard against dem faces, and your forehead hard against dem foreheads.
I don make your forehead like diamond, harder pass flint. No fear dem, neither dey dismayed at dem looks, though dem na rebellious house.”
Moreover e talk to me, “Son of man, all my words wey I go speak to you, receive for your heart, and hear with your ears.
Go, get to dem of di captivity, to di children of your people, and speak to dem, and tell dem, ‘Di Lord God talk like dis,’ whether dem hear, or whether dem refuse.”
Den di Spirit lift me up, and I hear behind me voice of great rushing, saying, “Blessed be di glory of di Lord from im place!”
I hear di noise of di wings of di living creatures wey touch one another, and di noise of di wheels beside dem, even noise of great rushing.
So di Spirit lift me up, and take me away. I go for bitterness, for di heat of my spirit, and di hand of di Lord dey strong upon me.
Den I come to dem of di captivity for Tel Abib, wey dwell by di river Chebar, and to where dem dey dwell. I sit dere overwhelmed among dem seven days.
E happen at di end of seven days, say di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“Son of man, I don make you watchman to di house of Israel. Therefore hear di word from my mouth, and give dem warning from me.

When I talk to di wicked, ‘You go surely die,’ and you no give am warning, nor speak to warn di wicked from im wicked way, to save im life, di same wicked man go die for im iniquity, but im blood I go require at your hand.
Yet if you warn di wicked, and e no turn from im wickedness, nor from im wicked way, e go die for im iniquity, but you don deliver your soul.

Again, when righteous man turn from im righteousness, and commit iniquity, and I lay stumbling block before am, e go die. Because you no give am warning, e go die for im sin, and im righteous deeds wey e don do go no dey remembered, but im blood I go require at your hand.
Nevertheless if you warn di righteous man, say di righteous man no go sin, and e no sin, e go surely live, because e take warning. Also you don deliver your soul.”
Di hand of di Lord dey dere on me, and e talk to me, “Arise, go forth into di plain, and dere I go speak with you.”
Den I arise, and go forth into di plain. See, di glory of di Lord dey stand dere, like di glory wey I see by di river Chebar. I fall on my face.
Den Spirit enter me, and set me on my feet. E speak with me, and talk to me, “Go, shut yourself inside your house.
But you, son of man, see, dem go put cords on you, and bind you with dem, and you no go go out among dem.
I go make your tongue cling to di roof of your mouth, so that you go dey mute, and no go be reprover to dem, because dem na rebellious house.
But when I speak with you, I go open your mouth, and you go talk to dem, ‘Di Lord God talk like dis.’ Im wey hear, make am hear. Im wey refuse, make am refuse, because dem na rebellious house.”
“You also, son of man, take tile, and lay am before you, and portray on am city, even Jerusalem.
Lay siege against am, and build siege wall against am, and cast mound against am. Set camps also against am, and set battering rams against am round about.
Take for yourself iron pan, and set am for wall of iron between you and di city. Set your face toward am, and e go dey besieged, and you go besiege am. Dis go be sign to di house of Israel.
Moreover lie on your left side, and lay di iniquity of di house of Israel on am. According to di number of di days wey you go lie on am, you go bear dem iniquity.
Because I don lay on you di years of dem iniquity, according to di number of di days, 390 days. So you go bear di iniquity of di house of Israel.
Again, when you don finish dis things, you go lie on your right side, and go bear di iniquity of di house of Judah. I don appoint you 40 days, each day for one year.
You go set your face toward di siege of Jerusalem, with your arm uncovered, and you go prophesy against am.
See, I go lay cords on you, and you no go turn from one side to another, until you don finish di days of your siege.

Take also for yourself wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet and spelt, and put dem for one vessel, and make bread of dem, according to di number of di days wey you go lie on your side. 390 days you go eat am.
Your food wey you go eat go dey by weight, 20 shekels a day. From time to time you go eat am.
You go drink water by measure, di sixth part of one hin. From time to time you go drink.
You go eat am as barley cakes, and you go bake am for dung wey dey come out of man, for dem sight.”
Di Lord talk, “Even so di children of Israel go eat dem bread unclean, among di nations where I go drive dem.”
Den I talk, “Ah Lord God! See, my soul no dey polluted, because from my youth up even till now I no eat wetin die by itself or dey torn by animals. Neither abominable meat don enter my mouth.”
Den e talk to me, “See, I don give you cow dung instead of man dung, and you go prepare your bread on am.”
Moreover e talk to me, “Son of man, see, I go break di staff of bread for Jerusalem. Dem go eat bread by weight, and with fearfulness. Dem go drink water by measure, and with dismay,
so that dem go lack bread and water, and dey dismayed one with another, and waste away for dem iniquity.”
“You, son of man, take sharp sword. Take am like barber razor, and cause am to pass over your head and over your beard. Den take balances to weigh, and divide di hair.

You go burn with fire one third inside di city, when di days of di siege don complete. You go take one third, and strike with di sword all round am. One third you go scatter to di wind, and I go draw out sword after dem.
You go take from dere small number, and bind dem for di skirts of your robe.
Of dem again you go take, and cast dem into di middle of di fire, and burn dem for di fire. From am fire go come out into all di house of Israel.
Di Lord God talk like dis: ‘Dis na Jerusalem. I don set am for di middle of di nations, and countries dey round about am.

She don rebel against my ordinances in wickedness more pass di nations, and against my statutes more pass di countries wey dey round about her, because dem don refuse my ordinances, and as for my statutes, dem no waka for dem.’

Therefore di Lord God talk like dis: ‘Because una dey more turbulent pass di nations wey dey round about una, and no waka for my statutes, neither keep my ordinances, neither do according to di ordinances of di nations wey dey round about una,
therefore di Lord God talk like dis: See, I, even I, dey against you. I go execute judgments for di middle of you for di sight of di nations.
I go do for you wetin I no do, and wetin I no go do any more like am, because of all your abominations.
Therefore fathers go eat dem sons for di middle of you, and sons go eat dem fathers. I go execute judgments on you, and all di remnant of you I go scatter to all di winds.

Therefore as I live,’ talk di Lord God, ‘surely, because you don defile my sanctuary with all your detestable things and with all your abominations, I go also diminish you. My eye no go spare, and I no go pity.

One third of you go die with di pestilence, and dem go dey consumed with famine for di middle of you. One third go fall by di sword round about you. One third I go scatter to all di winds, and I go draw out sword after dem.
Thus my anger go dey accomplished, and I go cause my wrath toward dem to rest, and I go dey comforted. Dem go know say I, di Lord, don speak am for my zeal, when I don accomplish my wrath on dem.
Moreover I go make you desolation and reproach among di nations wey dey round about you, for di sight of all wey pass by.

So e go be reproach and taunt, instruction and astonishment, to di nations wey dey round about you, when I don execute judgments on you in anger and in wrath, and in wrathful rebukes. I, di Lord, don speak am.
When I send on dem di evil arrows of famine, wey go be for destruction, wey I go send to destroy you, den I go increase famine on you, and break your staff of bread.
I go send on you famine and evil animals, and dem go bereave you. Pestilence and blood go pass through you. I go bring sword on you. I, di Lord, don speak am.’”
Di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“Son of man, set your face toward di mountains of Israel, and prophesy to dem,

and talk, ‘Mountains of Israel, hear di word of di Lord God! Di Lord God talk like dis to di mountains and to di hills, to di watercourses and to di valleys: See, I, even I, go bring sword on you, and I go destroy your high places.
Your altars go dey desolate, and your incense altars go dey broken. I go cast down your slain men before your idols.
I go lay di dead bodies of di children of Israel before dem idols. I go scatter your bones round about your altars.

For all your dwelling places di cities go dey laid waste, and di high places go dey desolate, so that your altars go dey laid waste and made desolate, and your idols go dey broken and cease, and your incense altars go dey cut down, and your works go dey abolished.
Di slain go fall for di middle of una, and una go know say I be di Lord.
Yet I go leave remnant, so that una go get some wey go escape di sword among di nations, when una dey scattered through di countries.

Dem wey escape of una go remember me among di nations where dem dey carried captive, how I dey broken with dem whoring heart, wey don depart from me, and with dem eyes, wey go whoring after dem idols. Dem go loathe demselves for di evils wey dem don commit for all dem abominations.
Dem go know say I be di Lord. I no talk in vain say I go do dis evil to dem.’”

Di Lord God talk like dis: “Strike with your hand, and stamp with your foot, and talk, ‘Alas, because of all di evil abominations of di house of Israel!’ Because dem go fall by di sword, by di famine, and by di pestilence.
Im wey dey far off go die of di pestilence. Im wey dey near go fall by di sword. Im wey remain, and dey besieged, go die by di famine. Na so I go accomplish my wrath on dem.

Una go know say I be di Lord, when dem slain men dey among dem idols round about dem altars, upon every high hill, on all di tops of di mountains, and under every green tree, and under every thick oak, di place where dem offer sweet incense to all dem idols.
I go stretch out my hand on dem, and make di land desolate and waste, from di wilderness toward Diblah, throughout all dem habitations. Den dem go know say I be di Lord.”
Moreover di word of di Lord come to me, say,
“You, son of man, di Lord God talk like dis to di land of Israel: ‘Di end! Di end don come on di four corners of di land.
Now di end dey on you, and I go send my anger on you, and go judge you according to your ways. I go bring on you all your abominations.
My eye no go spare you, neither I go have pity, but I go bring your ways on you, and your abominations go dey for your middle. Una go know say I be di Lord.’
Di Lord God talk like dis: ‘Disaster, singular disaster! See, e dey come.
Di end don come! Di end don come! E dey awake against you. See, e dey come.
Di doom don come to you, you wey dwell for di land. Di time don come. Di day dey near, day of tumult, and no joyful shouting of di mountains.
Now I go soon pour out my wrath on you, and accomplish my anger against you, and judge you according to your ways, and I go bring on you all your abominations.
My eye no go spare, neither I go have pity. I go repay you according to your ways, and your abominations go dey for your middle. Una go know say na I, di Lord, strike.
See, di day! See, e dey come. Di doom don go out. Di rod don blossom. Pride don bud.
Violence don rise up into rod of wickedness. None of dem go remain, none of dem multitude, none of dem wealth. Nothing of value go remain among dem.
Di time don come. Di day draw near. No make di buyer rejoice, nor di seller mourn, because wrath dey on all di multitude.
Because di seller no go return to wetin dem don sell, even though dem dey still alive, because di vision touch all di multitude. No one go return. No one go strengthen im life by im iniquity.
Dem don blow di trumpet, and don make all ready, but none dey go to di battle, because my wrath dey on all di multitude.
Di sword dey outside, and di pestilence and di famine dey inside. Im wey dey for di field go die by di sword. Im wey dey for di city, famine and pestilence go devour am.
But dem wey escape of dem go escape, and go dey on di mountains like doves of di valleys, all of dem mourning, everyone for im iniquity.
All hands go be feeble, and all knees go be weak as water.
Dem go also clothe dem with sackcloth, and horror go cover dem. Shame go dey on all faces, and baldness on all dem heads.

Dem go cast dem silver for di streets, and dem gold go be like unclean thing. Dem silver and dem gold no go fit deliver dem for di day of di wrath of di Lord. Dem no go satisfy dem souls, neither fill dem bowels, because e don be di stumbling block of dem iniquity.
As for di beauty of im ornament, e set am in majesty, but dem make di images of dem abominations and dem detestable things inside am. Therefore I don make am to dem like unclean thing.
I go give am into di hands of strangers for prey, and to di wicked of di earth for plunder. Dem go profane am.
I go turn my face from dem, and dem go profane my secret place. Robbers go enter inside am, and profane am.
Make chain, because di land dey full of bloody crimes, and di city dey full of violence.
Therefore I go bring di worst of di nations, and dem go possess dem houses. I go also make di pride of di strong to cease, and dem holy places go dey profaned.
Destruction dey come. Dem go seek peace, and e no go dey.
Disaster go come on disaster, and rumour go dey on rumour. Dem go seek vision of di prophet, but law go perish from di priest, and counsel from di elders.

Di king go mourn, and di prince go dey clothed with desolation, and di hands of di people of di land go tremble. I go do to dem after dem way, and according to dem own judgments I go judge dem. Dem go know say I be di Lord.’”
E happen for di sixth year, for di sixth month, for di fifth day of di month, as I sit for my house, and di elders of Judah sit before me, say di hand of di Lord God fall on me dere.
Den I look, and see, likeness as di appearance of fire. From di appearance of im waist and downward, fire, and from im waist and upward, like di appearance of brightness, like glowing metal.

E stretch out di form of hand, and take me by di lock of my head. Di Spirit lift me up between di earth and di heavens, and bring me in di visions of God to Jerusalem, to di entrance of di door of di gate of di inner court wey face toward di north, where di seat of di image of jealousy wey provoke to jealousy dey.
See, di glory of di God of Israel dey dere, according to di appearance wey I see for di plain.

Den e talk to me, “Son of man, lift up your eyes now di way toward di north.” So I lift up my eyes di way toward di north, and see, to di north of di gate of di altar dis image of jealousy for di entrance.

E talk to me, “Son of man, you see wetin dem dey do? Di great abominations wey di house of Israel dey commit here, so that I go go far off from my sanctuary? But you go still see greater abominations.”
E bring me to di door of di court. When I look, see, hole dey for di wall.
Den e talk to me, “Son of man, dig now for di wall.” When I don dig for di wall, see, door dey.
E talk to me, “Go in, and see di wicked abominations wey dem dey do here.”
So I go in and look, and see, every form of creeping things, and abominable animals, and all di idols of di house of Israel, portrayed on di wall round about.
Dere stand before dem 70 men of di elders of di house of Israel, and Jaazaniah, Shaphan pikin, stand among dem, with every man im censer for im hand. Di fragrance of di cloud of incense go up.

Den e talk to me, “Son of man, you don see wetin di elders of di house of Israel dey do for di dark, everyone for im rooms of imagery? Because dem talk, ‘Di Lord no see us. Di Lord don forsake di land.’”
E talk also to me, “You go still see greater abominations wey dem dey do.”
Den e bring me to di door of di gate of di Lord house wey dey toward di north, and see, women dey sitting dere weeping for Tammuz.
Den e talk to me, “You don see dis, son of man? You go still see greater abominations pass dis.”

E bring me into di inner court of di Lord house, and see, for di door of di temple of di Lord, between di porch and di altar, dey about 25 men, with dem backs toward di temple of di Lord, and dem faces toward di east. Dem dey worship di sun toward di east.

Den e talk to me, “You don see dis, son of man? E dey light thing to di house of Judah say dem commit di abominations wey dem commit here? Because dem don fill di land with violence, and don turn again to provoke me to anger. See, dem put di branch to dem nose.
Therefore I go also deal in wrath. My eye no go spare, neither I go have pity. Though dem cry in my ears with loud voice, yet I no go hear dem.”
Den e cry for my ears with loud voice, saying, “Cause dem wey dey in charge of di city to draw near, everyone with im destroying weapon for im hand.”

See, six men come from di way of di upper gate, wey face toward di north, everyone with im slaughter weapon for im hand. One man among dem dey clothed with linen, with writer inkhorn by im side. Dem go in, and stand beside di bronze altar.
Di glory of di God of Israel don go up from di cherub, where e dey, to di threshold of di house. E call to di man clothed with linen, wey get di writer inkhorn by im side.

Di Lord talk to am, “Go through di middle of di city, through di middle of Jerusalem, and set mark on di foreheads of di men wey sigh and wey cry because of all di abominations wey dem dey do for di middle of am.”
To di others e talk for my hearing, “Go through di city after am, and strike. Make una eye no spare, neither make una have pity.
Kill utterly old man, young man, maiden, little children and women, but no come near any man wey get di mark. Begin for my sanctuary.” Den dem begin with di old men wey dey before di house.
E talk to dem, “Defile di house, and fill di courts with di slain. Go out.” So dem go out, and strike for di city.
E happen, while dem dey striking, and I dey left, say I fall on my face, and cry, and talk, “Ah Lord God! You go destroy all di remnant of Israel for di pouring out of your wrath on Jerusalem?”

Den e talk to me, “Di iniquity of di house of Israel and Judah dey exceeding great. Di land dey full of blood, and di city full of perversity, because dem talk, ‘Di Lord don forsake di land, and di Lord no see.’
As for me also, my eye no go spare, neither I go have pity, but I go bring dem way on dem head.”
See, di man clothed with linen, wey get di inkhorn by im side, report di matter, saying, “I don do as you don command me.”
Den I look, and see, for di firmament wey dey over di head of di cherubim dey like sapphire stone, as di appearance of di likeness of throne wey appear above dem.

E talk to di man clothed with linen, “Go in between di whirling wheels, even under di cherub, and fill your hands with coals of fire from between di cherubim, and scatter dem over di city.” E go in for my sight.
Now di cherubim stand on di right side of di house, when di man go in, and di cloud fill di inner court.
Di glory of di Lord go up from di cherub, and stand over di threshold of di house. Di house dey filled with di cloud, and di court dey full of di brightness of di glory of di Lord.
Di sound of di wings of di cherubim dey heard even to di outer court, as di voice of God Almighty when e speak.
E happen say when e command di man clothed with linen, saying, “Take fire from between di whirling wheels, from between di cherubim,” say e go in, and stand beside di wheel.

Di cherub stretch out im hand from between di cherubim to di fire wey dey between di cherubim, and take some of am, and put am into di hands of di one wey dey clothed with linen, wey take am and go out.
Di cherubim appear to get di form of man hand under dem wings.
I look, and see, four wheels beside di cherubim, one wheel beside one cherub, and another wheel beside another cherub. Di appearance of di wheels dey like beryl stone.
As for dem appearance, di four of dem get one likeness, as if one wheel dey inside another wheel.
When dem go, dem go for dem four sides. Dem no turn as dem go, but to di place where di head face, dem follow am. Dem no turn as dem go.
Dem whole body, and dem backs, and dem hands, and dem wings, and di wheels dey full of eyes round about, even di wheels wey di four of dem get.
As for di wheels, dem dey call dem, for my hearing, “whirling wheels.”
Everyone get four faces. Di first face na di face of cherub, and di second face na face of man, and di third na face of lion, and di fourth na face of eagle.
Di cherubim dey lifted up. Dis na di living creature wey I see by di river Chebar.
When di cherubim go, di wheels go beside dem. When di cherubim lift up dem wings to mount up from di earth, di wheels no turn from beside dem.
When dem stand, di others stand. When dem dey lifted up, di others lift up demselves, because di spirit of di living creature dey inside dem.
Di glory of di Lord depart from off di threshold of di house, and stand over di cherubim.

Di cherubim lift up dem wings, and mount up from di earth for my sight when dem go out, with di wheels beside dem. Dem stand at di door of di east gate of di Lord house, and di glory of di God of Israel dey over dem above.
Dis na di living creature wey I see under di God of Israel by di river Chebar, and I know say dem na cherubim.
Everyone get four faces, and everyone four wings, and di likeness of man hands dey under dem wings.
As for di likeness of dem faces, dem na di faces wey I see by di river Chebar, dem appearance and dem selves. Dem go everyone straight forward.
